stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the example?
stimulus:
Crack Closure in Mortar Samples after 28 Days (% of crack width sealed)
Mortar type | 50% humidity | 95% humidity
Plain | 12 | 18
With bacterial spores | 15 | 71

Some engineers mix dormant bacterial spores into mortar so that the material can repair itself. When water seeps into a fresh crack, it revives the spores. The spores then turn a calcium-based nutrient packed into the mortar into calcite, which gradually fills the gap. Materials scientist Leilani Kahale and her colleagues compared plain mortar with spore-treated mortar at two humidity levels. They concluded that the advantage the spores provide depends heavily on available moisture: for example, ______
choices: at 95% humidity, mortar with spores sealed 71% of its crack width, whereas plain mortar sealed only 18%.
the spores raised crack closure by 53 percentage points at 95% humidity but by only 3 points at 50% humidity.
plain mortar sealed a larger share of its crack width at 95% humidity than it did at 50% humidity.
at 50% humidity, mortar with spores sealed a smaller share of its crack width than plain mortar did.
explanation: The claim is about the spores' advantage, meaning how much better spore-treated mortar does than plain mortar, and says that this advantage changes with moisture. To show it, you need the gap between the two mortar types at both humidity levels. At 95% humidity the gap is 71 − 18 = 53 points. At 50% humidity it is 15 − 12 = 3 points. Choice B gives both gaps, so it shows that the advantage is large when moisture is plentiful and nearly disappears when it is scarce.

A.why: This is an accurate reading of the table, but it covers only the high-humidity condition. It shows that the spores help when moisture is plentiful, but the claim is that their advantage depends on moisture. You can't show dependence without comparing the advantage across both humidity levels. You picked a true statement that doesn't prove the passage's point.

C.why: This is true (18% versus 12%), but it describes only plain mortar, which has no spores. The claim is about what the spores add, so a choice that leaves out the spore-treated samples can't support it. You matched the topic of moisture instead of the specific claim.

D.why: This misreads the table. At 50% humidity, mortar with spores sealed 15% of its crack width and plain mortar sealed 12%, so the spore-treated mortar did slightly better, not worse. Check the direction of each comparison against the numbers.
